title: Robjgrader
text: Automated grading student R scripts requires two things: capturing student’s script produces, checking whether objects meet substantive expectations. Existing tools handle one — way designed heterogeneous output political science methods course, single problem set might ask cleaned data frame, ggplot2 visualization, OLS fixed-effects model, formatted regression table. Robjgrader provides unified pipeline task. records every analytical object student’s script assigns prints, exposes flexible validation interface checks objects name, type, structural similarity reference solution — without requiring students follow fixed naming convention. Written answers can graded via LLM backend (Groq OpenAI-compatible endpoint), optional per-student feedback constrained constructive, precise, written plain English.

title: Robjgrader
Robjgrader
text: typical autograder script three stages: run_autograder() writes results /autograder/results/results.json (Gradescope format) prints summary console.
code: library(Robjgrader)  # 1. Record all objects produced by the student's script records <- source_student_file()  # 2. Validate individual objects res_df <- validate(records, "clean_data",   checks = list(nrow = 1000, required = c("year", "country", "gdp_pc")) )  res_model <- validate(records, "ols_model",   checks = list(estimator = "lm", required = c("gdp_pc", "polity2")) )  # 3. Run all test cases and write Gradescope-compatible JSON test_cases <- list(   list(name = "clean_data", result = res_df,    max_score = 20),   list(name = "ols_model",  result = res_model, max_score = 30) )  run_autograder(test_cases)

title: Robjgrader
text: Problem sets include written interpretation questions can graded via validate_text(), sends student’s answer OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (default: Groq). Pass question rubric grading prompt built automatically: feedback = TRUE, LLM returns short comment (max 3 sentences / 200 words) included Gradescope output incorrect answers. Feedback constrained prompt instructions constructive, precise, plain English — greetings, sign-offs, filler phrases. Text results integrate directly run_autograder() alongside object-based results, partial credit derived normalized score returned LLM:
code: answer <- find_student_text()          # auto-discovers the submission file  res_text <- validate_text(   text      = answer,   question  = "Interpret the coefficient on gdp_pc in your regression.",   rubric    = c(     direction    = "Correctly identifies the sign of the coefficient.",     magnitude    = "Interprets the substantive size of the effect.",     significance = "Mentions statistical significance and its implications."   ),   reference = "solution_q3.txt",       # optional model answer for comparison   feedback  = TRUE                     # include per-student written feedback ) test_cases <- list(   list(name = "OLS model",      result = res_model, max_score = 30),   list(name = "Interpretation", result = res_text,  max_score = 20) )  run_autograder(test_cases)
